skill.displayName: YouTube Creative Commons License Metadata — FlashData

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed FlashData integration for checking a YouTube license label, with network/API-key use that matches its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Network access to FlashData and paid Credits are necessary for the stated hosted data-query purpose and are clearly disclosed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation requires Python 3.10+, pinned mcp/httpx dependencies, and a FLASHDATA_API_KEY configured through the environment or secret manager.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions say to run only user-needed requests within approved budget, not execute examples on load, keep retrieved text untrusted, and avoid treating results as legal clearance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, privilege escalation, tool replacement, or broad filesystem access is present; optional async remote jobs are user-directed and documented.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is narrowly scoped to calling FlashData's youtube_trainability tool for a user-supplied YouTube video ID and explaining the returned Creative Commons label limitations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to send selected YouTube video IDs and your FlashData API key to FlashData, and set a budget because data queries can spend paid Credits. Keep the API key in protected environment settings, not prompts or files.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The external transmission finding is supported by the artifact, but the destination, API-key use, video_id arguments, costs, and purpose are disclosed and proportionate to the hosted FlashData MCP workflow.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no results, and local artifact review found no hidden execution, persistence, prompt hijacking, or destructive behavior.
